 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the appellant-claimant questioning the contributory negligence attributed on the rider of the motorcycle and also for the enhancement of compensation.
2. It is stated that on 09.11.2011 at 5.30 pm, the claimant along with his coolie were going to land in motorcycle bearing No.KA-24-K-5855.
When they reached near Watare village, at that time an Innova car bearing No.MH-09-BB-6077 coming from opposite side to the motorcycle dashed motorcycle and the pillion rider has sustained injuries.
Hence, claim petition is filed for claiming compensation under Section 166 of Motor vehicle Act, 1988.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
4.

In the present case, the Tribunal has held that the rider of the motorcycle has contributed 25% of rash and NC: 2023:KHC-D:10506 negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle for the reason that there were two pillion riders.
5. Upon considering the complaint, FIR, spot panchnama and charge sheet which proved that the entire allegations are made against the driver of innova car.
The driver of innova car is charge sheeted.
The motorcycle is found to be on it's correct side.
Innova car coming from opposite direction to the motorcycle in wrong side and hit the motorcycle.
Therefore, the entire rash and negligence is proved to be on the part of the driver of the innova car.
But the Tribunal is correct in holding that rider of the motorcycle had also contributed his negligence.
There were two pillion riders.
Hence, the rider of the motorcycle has also contributed to the accident to some extent but not at 25%.
Therefore, the rash and negligence aspect is considered as the driver of the innova car has contributed 85% and rider of motorcycle has contributed 15% of negligence.

To the above extent,
judgment and award is modified.

From the medical evidence on record, claimant has sustained the following injuries:
1. Fracture of right femur 2. Fracture of right tibia and fibula 3. Fracture of distal shaft of femur and 4. fracture of metacarpals i.e. 2nd , 4th and 5th of right hand.

3 7.

The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the various heads as below:
Sl. Particulars Amount(Rs.)
No.
1 Loss of future income 1,62,000-00 2 Pain and suffering 1,00,000-00 3 Loss of future amenities 25,000-00 4 Loss of life expectancy 15,000-00 5
Medical expenses 5,000-00 6
Towards conveyance, nourishment, 15,000-00  attendant charges 7 Loss of income during treatment 15,000-00  period

The quantum of compensation awarded under the head pain and suffering, loss of amenities,
medical expenses, towards incidental expenses and loss of income during treatment period are found to be just and proper.
In the present case, the doctor stated that the claimant had suffered 45% of physical disability towards right limb and the Tribunal considered 15% has functional disability towards whole body.
Considering functional disability is not a mathematical formula.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another1 issued guidelines regarding how to assess functional disability.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. The claimant is mason by profession and therefore, considering the nature of injury sustained as discussed above, disability suffered and avocation of the claimant as a mason, certainly the claimant has suffered significant functional disability affecting his work as mason for livelihood.

Therefore, it is just and proper to take 25% as functional disability affecting the earning capacity of the claimant since disability and that is to be compensated as per the judgment of Division Bench of this court in the case of New India Assurance Company vs. Abdul S/o (2011) 1 SCC 343 NC: 2023:KHC-D:10506 Mehaboob Tahasildar2 and as per decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sidram vs.
Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited and another3 and by following how much income is to be added by following the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi4 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.
11.

sentences.text: Claimant is aged 28 years old.
Hence, 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.
The accident is caused on 09.03.2011.
Therefore, notional income of Rs.6,000/- is taken.
The appropriate multiplier is 17 and functional disability is taken at 25%.
Therefore, the compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability is re-assessed and quantified as follows:

4 Rs.6,000/-+2400(40% of Rs.6,000/-)X25/100X17X12= Rs.4,28,400/-
MFA No.103807/2016 C/w. MFA Nos.103835/2016 & 103807/2018 (2023) 3 SCC 439 (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680 NC: 2023:KHC-D:10506 12.
The loss of life expectancy is covered under the above said head.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/-awarded by the tribunal towards loss of life expectancy is set aside.
13. Accordingly, compensation of Rs.4,28,400/- is awarded under the head loss of future income due to disability.

14. Thus, in all the appellant/claimant is entitled to a total compensation as determined by this Court is as follows:
Sl. Particulars Amount(Rs.)
No.
1 Loss of future income due to 4,28,000-00  disability.
2 Pain and suffering 1,00,000-00 3 Loss of future amenities 25,000-00 4
Medical expenses 5,000-00 5
Towards conveyance, nourishment, 15,000-00  attendant charges 6 Loss of income during treatment 15,000-00  period

Thus, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,88,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till realization of entire amount, as against Rs.3,37,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

16. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal filed by the claimant is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment award dated 05.02.2016 in MVC No.2272/2013 passed by V Addl.
District and Sessions Judge and MACT VI, Belagavi is hereby modified.
